cuts.reason: 5.1.4 repeats 5.5.1 and 5.5.2: the Level 2 recommendation is stated near-verbatim in 5.5.2 (D2); canonical home 1.5.1
cuts.text:
The three engagement levels in Section 5.5 change the **depth of the intelligence**, not the volume
of Firefly's output: how often the presence audit is refreshed, how many wards carry reach reporting,
how often creative is tested, and how far the team upskilling goes. They do
not change the list above, they never move a workstream from one owner to another, and they never
change Workstream 4 — accessibility applies in full at every level and is not a line to trade away
(Section 5.5.1).

**Firefly recommends Level 2 (Standard).** Level 1 instruments only the twelve decisive wards and
leaves the recognition deficit measured at county level, which is the one place this campaign cannot
afford to be blind. Level 3 refreshes the analysis faster than a nomination sprint can act on it.
Standard is the level at which all 40 wards carry both reach reporting and an active SMS and USSD
layer — and reaching the arid belt is the whole argument.

pointers.text: The compliance gate, and the fallback the model runs on until it clears, are set out in 5.3.4.
The decision first: what is being asked, what Dr. Mulu receives and at which level, who does what, and what the campaign must decide or provide.
How the three engagement levels change what runs, and the Level 2 recommendation, are set out once, in 1.5.1.
The indicators themselves are set out in 5.1.
How the engagement is run, when and by whom: the weekly operating rhythm, the first weeks, the phases to August 2027 and the coalition calendar.
The two scope lists below stay together, rather than being split across the workstreams that deliver them, until conflict C4 is settled.
The four content pillars are now in 3.2.3, with the other production pillars. Formats by channel and the radio, SMS and USSD copy samples are in Annex G.2.
The languages this standard works in, and the content mix for locally facing platforms, are set out in 3.6.1.
The platform-by-platform playbooks (Facebook, X, WhatsApp, TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and Google Ads) are in Annex G.1.
The volunteer programme reference (tiers, gamification, tooling and KPIs) is in Annex G.3.
The Data Protection Act obligations this layer works under, and its mandatory compliance safeguards, are set out with the rest of compliance in 5.3.2.
The data sources the model draws on are listed in Annex G.5.
The model's variable dictionary is in Annex G.5.
The reference architecture the campaign owns (component by component, the procurement matrix and the technical security protocols) is in Annex G.4.
Who does the work: the Firefly core, the surge roles activated by phase and level, and how the existing team is assessed and upskilled.
How progress is measured, how the Week 1 presence audit is run, and how the work is kept lawful.
Analysis of the rivals themselves is in 2.6.4; the tools and outputs are in Annex E.4 and E.12.
The field itself is analysed in 2.6; each line below records the documents a rival's attributes rest on.
Who this proposal is for, who prepared it, and its status are stated once, on the cover.

ANNEX G. Channel and technical specifications: the platform playbooks, formats and copy samples, the volunteer programme reference, the technology reference architecture, and the voter model's data sources and variables. Reference the main text points to, not argues from.
